3. WHERE ALPACA SITS: attach mode
Your code stays in its own repo with its own history. Alpaca keeps its notes, records and

4. CHECKS
Each of these is a gate (a command that must pass before a change can leave the studio). I run
every gate on your current main first, so a gate that already fails there is not blamed on new
work.
- py-syntax: the 6 Python files parse. Tried it: pass, 0.05 s [9]
- cmake-configure: CMake still configures with this machine's compiler. Not tried yet: it runs
  your CMake files, so it runs only after your yes [1]
- arm-syntax (suggested by me): 23 C files type-check against the ST headers for the Cortex-M4.
  It skips main.c and 6 app files, which need an ARM C library this machine lacks. Tried it:
  pass, 0.89 s [12]

6. HOW A CHANGE REACHES YOUR REPO
Each task (one small piece of work with its own branch) gets its own branch, named alpaca/ and

branch and on a trial merge with the newest main. You approve the exact commit. This repo is not
on GitHub, so I cannot send the branch for you: I give you the branch and you send it where you
send changes today. Your repo will show this of me; tell me any line to change:

- Branch prefix: alpaca/ (my default; it names Alpaca)

7. HOW MUCH I DO ALONE: L2
